author: BBC News
description:
French President Emmanuel Macron has called for "calm and order" after a major day of protests turned into rioting and looting on Saturday, and as some disorder continued in Paris on Sunday.
 
In a national address from the Élysée Palace, he warned those who had taken part not to "escalate", adding: "We all feel anger and shame."
 
Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for largely peaceful protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.
 
Macron said a distinction must be drawn between the "legitimate demands" of protesters and "those who destroyed, smashed and looted".
 
Police have arrested about 2,400 people, according to France's interior ministry.

title: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after weekend of protests and disorder in France | BBC News

author: BBC News
description:
The French President Emmanuel Macron has said violent protesters will face justice, after the worst unrest for decades.   2,400 people have been arrested and almost 1,000 police officers injured, as buildings were burned and shops looted in the protests over high prices and problems with public serves. 

More clashes have broken out in Paris and Marseille, where riot police intervened to prevent attempts to ransack businesses.  Nationwide demonstrations had earlier erupted into riots, with a town hall burned, shops pillaged and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.

“Looking at these images, we have all asked ourselves: What was going through their minds? How can French people do this to France?" Macron said in a televised address to the nation. "Nothing justifies it, nothing explains it, nothing excuses it. Tonight, we all feel anger and shame."

Violence broke out across France on Saturday during the latest day of demonstrations against hardship in schools and the cost of living.
 
At least 1,200 people were arrested during what the French government described as an "escalation in violence" alongside an estimated 550,000 taking to the streets.
 
In Paris, there were significant clashes into the evening with riot police, who used tear gas and water cannon on crowds.

author: BBC News
description:
Several people have been killed or injured as a result of a large fire near a Canadian military base in Alberta, the nation's defence minister has said.
 
David McGuinty did not confirm the cause or the number of casualties, describing the situation as "very, very active and delicate". The Canadian military and local authorities were managing the fire, he said.
 
Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, where the fire broke out, is one of the country's busiest military training bases.
